mainTopic: Inheriting from a mother: does a son come before a daughter, and how is that learned?
overview: A ברייתא proves from the plural word 'tribes' in a פסוק that a daughter inherits from her mother. A קל וחומר then shows that a son inherits from his mother too. The תנא קמא says the son even comes before the daughter, while רבי זכריה בן הקצב says they share equally because of the rule of דיו. The גמרא asks how the תנא קמא can ignore דיו, which is learned from the story of מרים's seven days. It answers that the son's precedence comes from a הקש in ״ממטות״, not from the קל וחומר. A series of stories shows that רב נחמן and שמואל refused to let judges rule like רבי זכריה, and the גמרא explains that רב and שמואל both rejected his view. Finally, רבי יהודה נשיאה asks רבי ינאי for the source that a son comes first in the mother's property. When רבי ינאי gives the הקש, he challenges it: then a בכור should take a double portion of his mother's property too. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A daughter inherits from two tribes, so she inherits from her mother
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the plural 'tribes' in the פסוק as a daughter whose father and mother came from different tribes. When both die, she inherits from both, so a daughter inherits from her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Every daughter who inherits from the tribes of Israel.' How can one daughter inherit from two tribes? It must mean a girl whose father is from one tribe and whose mother is from another. Both parents died, and she inherited from both.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens by proving from a פסוק that a daughter inherits her mother's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'tribes' is plural, yet a person belongs to only one tribe through her father. The only way she can inherit from two tribes is if she also inherits from her mother, who is from a different tribe. This sets up the basic rule that a בת inherits from her mother.

phrases.english: "And every daughter who possesses an inheritance
from the tribes of the children of Israel"
How can a daughter inherit from two tribes?
Rather, this is one whose father is from one tribe
and her mother is from another tribe,
and they died, and she inherited from them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter inherits her mother's property, learned from the plural 'tribes' in the פסוק.

steps.title: What about a son?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only spoke about a daughter. Where do we learn that a son also inherits from his mother?
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about a daughter. Where do I learn it for a son?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks where we learn that a son inherits from his mother. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only mentioned a בת, so the son's right to his mother's property still needs a source. The ברייתא is asking for that source.

phrases.english: I have derived only a daughter;
from where do I derive a son?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּת, בֵּן מִנַּיִן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a son inherits from his mother.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the daughter to the son
steps.stepSummary: A daughter is weak with her father's property, yet she inherits her mother's. A son is strong with his father's property, so surely he inherits his mother's.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can make a קל וחומר. A daughter has weaker rights in her father's property (a son comes first), yet she has strong rights in her mother's property. A son has strong rights in his father's property. Isn't it logical that he also has strong rights in his mother's property?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question with a קל וחומר: if the weaker daughter inherits from the mother, the stronger son certainly does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a father's estate, a son takes everything and the daughter gets nothing, so the son is 'stronger.' If even the 'weaker' daughter inherits her mother, the 'stronger' son should inherit her too. This gives the son a source.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger case

phrases.english: You can say an a fortiori inference:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בַּת, שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחָהּ בְּנִכְסֵי הָאָב –
phrases.english: Just as a daughter, whose power is weakened in the father's property,
phrases.notes: She is 'weakened' because if there is a son, she gets nothing from her father.

phrases.english: has strong power in the mother's property;
a son, whose power is strong in the father's property,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחוֹ בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם?
phrases.english: is it not logical that his power is strong in the mother's property?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the daughter: if she inherits her mother, the stronger son surely does.

steps.title: The תנא קמא: the son comes before the daughter
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא adds that the son comes first in the mother's property too, just as he comes first in the father's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where you started: just as there, with the father's property, a son comes before a daughter, so too here, with the mother's property, a son comes before a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא קמא now says the son does not just inherit the mother. He actually comes before the daughter, the same as with a father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר was built on the son's strength in the father's property. The תנא קמא carries over that full strength: the son takes first and the daughter gets nothing. This goes further than the source case, where the daughter does inherit.

keyTerms.meaning: And from the place you came from (the source of the argument)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'There' is the father's property, where a son already comes first. 'Here' is the mother's property, which is what we are learning about.

phrases.english: And from the place that you came:
phrases.notes: He means: from the father's property, the case the קל וחומר started from.

phrases.english: just as there, a son precedes a daughter,
so too here, a son precedes a daughter.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a son comes before a daughter in inheriting the mother's property.

steps.title: רבי זכריה בן הקצב: son and daughter are equal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, quoting רבי זכריה בן הקצב, say a son and a daughter share the mother's property equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said in the name of רבי זכריה בן הקצב: a son and a daughter are equal in the mother's property.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with the תנא קמא and says the son does not come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that a son inherits his mother. The argument is only about whether he pushes out the daughter. Here he does not; they split the property equally.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, said
in the name of Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav:
Both the son and the daughter
are equal in the mother's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד הַבֵּן וְאֶחָד הַבַּת, שָׁוִין בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling that the son comes first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son and a daughter inherit the mother's property equally.

steps.title: His reason: דיו
steps.stepSummary: The reason is the rule of דיו: what you learn through a קל וחומר can be no stronger than the case you learned it from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is enough for the thing learned from the argument to be like the thing it was learned from.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why רבי זכריה בן הקצב makes them equal: the rule of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's right came only from the daughter's right, through a קל וחומר. By דיו, the result can't go beyond the source. The daughter in the source inherits, so the son cannot push her out; he can only be equal to her.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for the conclusion of a קל וחומר to be like its source

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument is about דיו. The תנא קמא gives the son full strength and he comes first. רבי זכריה בן הקצב applies דיו, so the son is only equal to the daughter.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is sufficient for that which comes from the inference
to be like the source.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle of דיו limits the son to the daughter's level, so they are equal.
steps.whyThisMatters: דיו is a basic rule for how a קל וחומר works, and it comes up all over the תלמוד.

steps.title: How can the תנא קמא ignore דיו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: does he not use דיו? But דיו comes from the Torah!
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא does not use the rule of דיו?! But דיו comes from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the תנא קמא's view, since it seems to break the rule of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If דיו is a Torah rule, every תנא should accept it. Yet the תנא קמא let the son come first, which goes beyond the source case of the daughter. The גמרא wants to know how he can do that.

keyTerms.meaning: The first opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: And the first tanna does not expound "it is sufficient"?!
But "it is sufficient" is from the Torah!

steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling that a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Letting the son come first goes beyond the source case, which breaks דיו. דיו is a Torah rule, so the תנא קמא should not be able to ignore it.

steps.title: The Torah source for the rule of דיו: מרים's seven days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that דיו is in the Torah itself. By קל וחומר, מרים should have been sent out for fourteen days, but she was sent out for only seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: How does a קל וחומר work? ה׳ said to משה: 'If her father had spit in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days?' Then by קל וחומר, when the שכינה is the one who rebuked her, it should be fourteen days! Instead, it is enough for what you learn from a קל וחומר to be like its source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge from step 7. It brings a ברייתא showing that the rule of דיו is written right into a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father's rebuke brings seven days of shame. A rebuke from the שכינה is far more serious, so a קל וחומר would give fourteen days. The Torah gives only seven, which proves the rule of דיו: the result can't be stronger than its source. So how can the תנא קמא ignore it?

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a lighter case to a more serious one

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like the case it was learned from

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes דיו a Torah-based rule, not just a matter of logic. That is why the תנא קמא must explain why he doesn't follow it here.

phrases.english: As it is taught: how does a kal vachomer work?
"And ה׳ said to Moshe:
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:14. This is about מרים, after she spoke against משה.

phrases.english: If her father had spit in her face,
would she not be ashamed for seven days?"
All the more so for the Divine Presence: fourteen days!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן.
phrases.english: Rather, it is enough for what comes from the inference to be like its source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that powers the קשיא of step 7
steps.raayaObject: That דיו is a Torah rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 12:14, the seven days of מרים

steps.title: The תנא קמא uses דיו, but a הקש from ״ממטות״ overrides it here
steps.stepSummary: In general the תנא קמא does use דיו. Here, though, the word ״ממטות״ links the mother's property to the father's, so a son comes first in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: In general, he does use דיו. But here it is different, because the פסוק says 'from the tribes'. It compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe. Just as with the father's tribe a son comes before a daughter, so too with the mother's tribe a son comes before a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The תנא קמא's rule that the son comes first does not come from the קל וחומר but from a הקש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word ״ממטות״ (tribes) hints at two tribes, the father's and the mother's, and sets them side by side. Because of this הקש, the father's rule that a son comes first carries over to the mother. The precedence is learned from the הקש, not the קל וחומר, so the limit of דיו does not hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, links two things through a הקש
Tribe; here, a family line one inherits from

steps.confusionAlert: The תנא קמא does not reject דיו. He agrees with it in general and only says it doesn't apply here, because his source is a הקש, not a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: In general he does interpret using "it is enough";
but here it is different, as the verse says: "from the tribes"
It compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe;

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַטֵּה הָאָב – בֵּן קוֹדֵם לַבַּת,
phrases.english: just as with the father's tribe, a son comes before a daughter,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַטֵּה הָאֵם – בֵּן קוֹדֵם לַבַּת.
phrases.english: so too with the mother's tribe, a son comes before a daughter.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: a הקש instead of a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא relies on a קל וחומר and so ignores דיו
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא learns from the הקש of ״ממטות״, so דיו is not relevant

steps.title: שמואל stops רב ניתאי from ruling like רבי זכריה
steps.stepSummary: רב ניתאי wanted to rule like רבי זכריה בן הקצב, who said a son and a daughter share equally. שמואל told him רבי זכריה's view counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ניתאי thought to rule in a real case like רבי זכריה בן הקצב. שמואל said to him: Like whom? Like זכריה? זכריה is nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from theory to practice. It tells a story showing that רבי זכריה's opinion is not followed as הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זכריה's opinion (step 5) was that a son and a daughter share the mother's property equally. שמואל's sharp reply, 'זכריה is nothing', means this view is not accepted at all for a real ruling. The הלכה is like the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: To act on it, to rule in a real case

phrases.english: Rav Nittai thought to rule in a real case
in accordance with Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav;
phrases.notes: He is the one from step 5 who said a son and a daughter share equally.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to him: Like whom? Like Zekharya?
Zekharya is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נִיתַּאי סָבַר לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא כְּרַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining the opinions to how we actually rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not rule like רבי זכריה בן הקצב

steps.title: רב נחמן orders רבי טבלא to take back his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא did rule like רבי זכריה, relying on a report in the name of רב. רב נחמן told him to take it back and threatened to punish him harshly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבלא ruled in a real case like רבי זכריה בן הקצב. רב נחמן said to him: What is this? He answered: רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב that the הלכה is like רבי זכריה בן הקצב. רב נחמן said to him: Go take it back. If not, I will pull רב חיננא בר שלמיא out of your ear!
steps.whatsHappening: A second story makes the same point. Even when someone quotes רב in support, a ruling like רבי זכריה must be taken back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טבלא had a source: a report from רב that the הלכה follows רבי זכריה. רב נחמן rejects it firmly and demands that the ruling be undone. His colorful threat means he would punish him severely. The final word: a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property too.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the תנא קמא: a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property, just like the father's. The source is the הקש of ״ממטות״, so דיו doesn't limit it. רבי זכריה's view of equal shares is rejected in practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tavla ruled in a real case
in accordance with Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: מַאי הַאי?
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: He said to him: As Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelamya said in the name of Rav:
The halacha is like Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav.
He said to him: Go take back your ruling,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, he means 'retract'.

phrases.english: and if not, I will pull out for you
Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelamya from your ear!
phrases.notes: A sharp way of saying: I will punish you hard for relying on that report.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַבְלָא עֲבַד עוֹבָדָא כְּרַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that confirms the rejection from step 10, even against a quote from רב
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is not like רבי זכריה בן הקצב. A son comes before a daughter in inheriting from the mother.

steps.title: רב הונא בר חייא wants to rule like רבי זכריה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא planned to rule like רבי זכריה בן הקצב. When רב נחמן questioned him, he quoted רב הונא in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא wanted to give a real ruling like רבי זכריה בן הקצב. רב נחמן asked him, 'What is this?' He answered: 'רב הונא said in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי זכריה בן הקצב.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third story, just like the story of רבי טבלא. A judge wants to rule like רבי זכריה, and רב נחמן asks him what he is basing it on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי טבלא before him, רב הונא בר חייא relies on a report from רב. This time the report comes through רב הונא, who is still alive. That detail sets up רב נחמן's sharp reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To do an action, meaning to give a real, practical ruling
What is this? A sharp question showing disapproval

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא סָבַר לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiyya thought to perform an action
phrases.notes: 'Perform an action' means he wanted to actually rule this way in a real case.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rabbi Zecharya ben HaKatzav;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: מַאי הַאי?
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: He said to him: As Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Zecharya ben HaKatzav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא סָבַר לְמֶעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא כְּרַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story, parallel to רבי טבלא's ruling in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בר חייא claims, through רב הונא, that רב ruled like רבי זכריה בן הקצב.

steps.title: רב נחמן exposes the shaky report
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן offers to send a messenger to check with רב הונא. רב הונא בר חייא is embarrassed, and רב נחמן scolds him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said, 'Should I send someone to ask רב הונא?' רב הונא בר חייא was embarrassed. רב נחמן said, 'Now, if רב הונא had already passed away, you would be bold enough to say this to my face.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects the report by offering to check it with רב הונא, who is still alive. The judge is embarrassed because he cannot really back up what he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב הונא is alive, the claim can easily be checked, and the embarrassment shows it would not hold up. רב נחמן's point is that a dubious quote can only be passed off when the source is no longer around to deny it. So the report from רב is thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall I send to him? Meaning: shall I check with him directly?
His soul rested, meaning he passed away
You would have been brazen, bold enough to say it

phrases.english: He said to him: Shall I send to him?
phrases.notes: רב נחמן means he will send a messenger to ask רב הונא himself whether he really said this.

phrases.english: He was embarrassed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Now, if Rav Huna had passed away,
you would have been brazen before me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the report quoted in step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב ruled like רבי זכריה בן הקצב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report could not be confirmed. The speaker's embarrassment shows he could not stand behind it when it could be checked.

steps.title: What is רב נחמן's own source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what opinion רב נחמן relied on when he rejected רבי זכריה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion did he (רב נחמן) follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב נחמן based himself on when he refused to rule like רבי זכריה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some sages did rule like רבי זכריה, and רב נחמן blocked them strongly. The גמרא wants to know what authority stood behind his firm position.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion does he hold like?

phrases.english: And he, in accordance with whom does he hold?
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רב נחמן, who rejected both judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב נחמן's rejections in steps 11 and 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which authority רב נחמן relied on in rejecting רבי זכריה בן הקצב

steps.title: רב and שמואל both reject רבי זכריה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן follows רב and שמואל, who both say the הלכה does not follow רבי זכריה בן הקצב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רב and שמואל, who both said: the הלכה does not follow רבי זכריה בן הקצב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן relied on a statement that both רב and שמואל made: the הלכה is not like רבי זכריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the matter. The reports claiming רב ruled like רבי זכריה are unreliable, because רב himself, together with שמואל, ruled the other way. So a son comes before a daughter, even in the mother's property.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a son comes before a daughter in inheriting the mother's property too, and we do not rule like רבי זכריה בן הקצב, who said they share equally.

phrases.english: Like this statement of Rav and Shmuel,
who both say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב.
phrases.english: The halacha does not follow Rabbi Zecharya ben HaKatzav.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן follows רב and שמואל, who both rule against רבי זכריה בן הקצב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב's real position goes against the reports that רבי טבלא and רב הונא בר חייא relied on.

steps.title: רבי ינאי feels the נשיא's cloak
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי, leaning on his attendant רבי שמלאי, meets רבי יהודה נשיאה. רבי שמלאי praises the cloak, but רבי ינאי feels it and says it is as coarse as sackcloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי was walking, leaning on the shoulder of his attendant רבי שמלאי, and רבי יהודה נשיאה came toward them. רבי שמלאי said: 'The man coming toward us is handsome, and his cloak is handsome.' When he reached them, רבי ינאי felt the cloak and said: 'This one's measure is like sackcloth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the meeting between רבי ינאי and רבי יהודה נשיאה. In that meeting, a question about a son and a daughter inheriting from the mother will come up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמלאי saw only the outside and called the cloak fine. רבי ינאי touched it and judged it coarse and thick, like sackcloth. The story leads straight into the inheritance discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Its measure is like sackcloth, meaning it is coarse material

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai was walking, leaning
on the shoulder of Rabbi Simlai, his attendant,
and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia came toward them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּר אִינָשׁ דַּאֲתָא לְקִיבְלַנָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: The person who is coming toward us,
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רבי שמלאי, describing to רבי ינאי what he sees.

phrases.english: he is handsome, and his cloak is handsome.
When he reached him, he felt it,
He said to him: This one, its measure is like sackcloth.
phrases.notes: רבי ינאי means the cloak is thick and rough, like sackcloth, so it is not fine at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיסְתְּמִיךְ וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי יַנַּאי אַכַּתְפָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי שַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, which leads into the source for a son coming first in the mother's property
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי judges רבי יהודה נשיאה's cloak to be coarse, like sackcloth.

steps.title: Source that a son comes first in the mother's property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks רבי ינאי where we learn that a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: From where do we know that a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks רבי ינאי for the source of the rule that a son inherits before a daughter when the mother dies. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier verses teach the order of inheritance from a father. The question is how we know the same order applies to a mother's property.

phrases.english: He asked him:
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה נשיאה is asking רבי ינאי.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְבֵן שֶׁקּוֹדֵם לַבַּת בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם?
phrases.english: From where do we know that a son precedes a daughter in the mother's property?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ: מִנַּיִן לְבֵן שֶׁקּוֹדֵם לַבַּת בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The conversation that follows the meeting in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for a son coming before a daughter in the mother's inheritance

steps.title: The word מטות links mother to father
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that the plural ״מטות״ compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe. Just as a son comes first with the father, he comes first with the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: It says ״מטות״, 'tribes'. The verse compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe. Just as with the father's tribe a son comes before a daughter, so too with the mother's tribe a son comes before a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי gives the source. The plural word ״מטות״ links the mother's inheritance to the father's, so the same order of inheritance applies to both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a היקש, a comparison the פסוק makes by putting two things together. Because they are compared, the rule of the father (son first) carries over to the mother. This is the same source the גמרא used in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, linking two things so that one's rules apply to the other (a היקש)

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written: “Tribes”
it compares the tribe of the mother to the tribe of the father;

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַטֵּה הָאָב – בֵּן קוֹדֵם לַבַּת,
phrases.english: just as with the father's tribe, a son precedes a daughter,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַטֵּה הָאֵם – בֵּן קוֹדֵם לַבַּת.
phrases.english: so too with the mother's tribe, a son precedes a daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״מַטּוֹת״ – מַקִּישׁ מַטֵּה הָאֵם לְמַטֵּה הָאָב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural ״מטות״ compares the mother's tribe to the father's, so a son comes first in both.

steps.title: Then a firstborn should get double from the mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה challenges him: if the mother is fully compared to the father, a בכור should also take a double portion of the mother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, then just as with the father's tribe a בכור takes a double portion, so too with the mother's tribe a בכור should take a double portion!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה pushes back on the comparison. If the mother is like the father, then the double portion of the בכור should apply to her property too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש normally carries over the rules of one side to the other. So if it moves the 'son first' rule, it should also move the בכור's double portion. Yet a בכור does not get a double portion from his mother, so the comparison seems to prove too much.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי – מָה מַטֵּה הָאָב,
phrases.english: He said to him: If so, just as with the father's tribe,
a firstborn takes a double portion;

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַטֵּה הָאֵם, בְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם?!
phrases.english: so too with the mother's tribe, a firstborn should take a double portion?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי – מָה מַטֵּה הָאָב, בְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the היקש given in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's comparison of the mother's tribe to the father's from ״מטות״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the היקש is complete, every inheritance rule of the father should carry over, including the בכור's double portion. That result is not accepted, so the היקש seems to prove too much.
